extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, newsroom managers, journalists, and the general public interested in news trust/transparency standards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for news organizations to disclose the integrity behind journalism via the Trust Project's 8 Trust Indicators, including technical, editorial, membership, and complaint-handling requirements so outlets can demonstrate trustworthiness and use the Trust Mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of trustworthy news
rubrics_metrics.description: News that is accurate, accountable and ethically produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short definition used by the Trust Project to describe the end goal of the indicators. The Project helps make it easy for people to identify journalism with integrity so the public can make informed news choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust Indicators (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight standardized disclosures about the news outlet, the journalist, and the policies that keep them focused on the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are transparency disclosures designed to show who and what is behind a given story — the standards, policies and expertise that ensure honest journalism. They were developed via user-centered design with news executives and public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of news organization information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information about the company, its standards and policies, and ownership structure so readers can understand who is behind coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Trust Project partner sites, readers will find a link to information about the company and important information about partner policies and ownership structure on dedicated pages. The disclosures should be visible across article pages and partner listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of journalist identity and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details about the journalist who produced the story and links to find out more about their expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each article page should include a link to information about the journalist; special pages should describe individual journalists' expertise. Providing journalist details increases confidence in the reporter and the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear labeling of content type (opinion/analysis/paid/reported)
rubrics_metrics.description: Label pieces clearly when they are opinion, analysis, or paid content rather than reported, impartial news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear label with a definition should appear on article pages and in broadcasts, podcasts and video when applicable so audiences can understand the nature of the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source transparency on in-depth or controversial pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: On more in-depth or potentially controversial news pieces, disclose the sources used to get to the facts or to understand a complicated issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information about sources and how the story was built. This transparency responds to users' desire to know 'how the story was built' and helps distinguish trustworthy journalism from other information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of newsroom policies and expertise pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Make newsroom policies and pages describing journalists' expertise discoverable and linked from article pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special pages should describe policies and individual journalists' expertise; partners display the Trust Indicators within their own design environment but should ensure access to these explanatory pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-readable implementation (Trust Project Schema.org vocabulary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers must add the Trust Project-Schema.org vocabulary to their page code so indicators are represented as machine-readable signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital platforms (Google, Facebook, Bing) use the Trust Indicators and their machine-readable signals in various ways. Publishers are responsible for adding the vocabulary; the Trust Project internal team helps with UX or technical compliance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility and editorial commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Only established news organizations producing a majority of original journalism and committing to accuracy, multiple perspectives, correction of mistakes, and public service as their central mission can join.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User-generated content and discussion are allowed as components but cannot be the site's sole purpose. This set of commitments forms the baseline for Trust Project membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting and approval process for partners
rubrics_metrics.description: News sites must undergo a multi-step approval process including an application, review, implementation guidance, and compliance checks before being approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: fill out an application form, attend a prospective partners' meeting, be reviewed for qualification (with explanation if not approved), be placed in an implementation cohort if approved, implement indicators with guidance, and pass a final compliance check before going live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing compliance checks and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved sites are checked for compliance before going live and rechecked on an ad hoc basis; false claims of participation are addressed by the Trust Project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compliance or false claims are found, the Trust Project internal team works with the site to fix issues. The Project provides information to external partners about which sites are in good standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust Mark eligibility and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Mark indicates a news organization is confirmed by the Trust Project to be compliant with all 8 Trust Indicators and has completed the training program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating sites may show the Trust Mark on pages where they describe standards/practices and on article pages, and may use it on air and in videos and podcasts. Only approved and fully compliant sites may show the Trust Mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint adjudication and remediation process
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential complaint adjudication process evaluates serious complaints about news partner behavior, reviews facts, allows the site to respond, and can remove the Trust Mark if no resolution is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Trust Mark is removed, there is an opportunity for appeal within one month and reapplication after one year. The process is intended to hold partners accountable and ensure resolution of serious issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting channel and partner commitment to feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public should report concerns or suggestions about coverage via the news partners page; partners commit to listening to feedback and advice from the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Project asks the public to report concerns using the news partners page; the Project and its partners agree that public accountability helps uphold high journalistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-centered design and research basis for indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators must be responsive to public needs and reflect core journalism values, having been developed from one-on-one user interviews and workshops with news executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Indicators emerged from iterative research (interviews, workshops, working groups) to ensure they address what people value in news and can be recognized anywhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-medium implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Indicators should be visible and applied across mediums including article pages, broadcasts, podcasts and video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators are referenced in broadcasts, podcasts and video as well as on web article pages; partners should ensure consistent presentation of indicators across formats.
